phone.definition: a device used for talking to other people over a distance.
examples: Please answer the phone.

play.definition: a form of activities for enjoyment or for a performance; a game.
examples: We watched a play at the theater.

player.definition: a person who plays a game or instrument; a participant in a sport.
examples: The pianist is a skilled player.

playing.definition: the action of taking part in a game or activity.
examples: Playing with friends helps social skills.

playful.definition: full of fun and playful; fond of games.
examples: The kitten is playful this afternoon.

parade.definition: a public procession to celebrate or honor something.
examples: They watched the parade from the sidewalk.

plane.definition: a powered flying vehicle with wings.
examples: They flew on a plane to Paris.

pleased.definition: liked what happened or what one received; satisfied.
examples: We are pleased with your effort.

painting.definition: the act or art of making pictures with paint; the picture itself.
examples: She finished the painting yesterday.

parents.definition: the people who have given birth to or raised a child.
examples: My parents watched my game.

pop.definition: short for popular music; a light, upbeat genre.
examples: She danced to pop on the radio.

perform.definition: to carry out, accomplish, or enact; to present a form of entertainment.
examples: They perform in a theater group.

performer.definition: a person who performs, especially in front of an audience.
examples: The performer sang beautifully.

performance.definition: the act of performing or presenting something; how well something works.
examples: Her performance earned praise.

performing.definition: the act of performing; currently in progress.
examples: Performing requires confidence.

party.definition: a group of people gathered for a particular purpose; a social gathering.
examples: We attended a party last night.

pasta.definition: a type of Italian noodle food made from wheat flour and water.
examples: We had pasta for lunch.

piano.definition: a keyboard musical instrument that makes sound when strings are struck by hammers.
examples: He learned to play the piano.

park.definition: a large public area of land for relaxation and recreation; trees and grass.
examples: The park is crowded on weekends.

pants.definition: a piece of clothing worn on the lower body; typically covering the legs.
examples: Pants are drying on the line.

petrified.definition: so frightened that one is unable to move; terrified.
examples: They stood petrified at the edge of the cliff.

pliers.definition: a small tool used for bending and cutting wire.
examples: The electrician used pliers carefully.
That is a pretty necklace.
The expedition faced perilous weather.
She is a powerful speaker.

perspicacious.definition: Having a ready insight into and understanding of things; very perceptive.
examples: A perspicacious reader notices details others miss.

petrichor.definition: The pleasant smell that accompanies the first rain after a dry spell.
examples: The petrichor after the storm filled the air.

pigment.definition: To color or tint with pigment.
examples: The cloth was pigmented with natural colors.

placid.definition: Calm and peaceful; not easily upset.
examples: The lake looked placid at dawn.

psalm.definition: A sacred hymn or song used in worship.
examples: They sang a psalm during the service.

psychology.definition: The scientific study of the mind and behavior.
examples: She studied psychology to understand human behavior.

portal.definition: a website or online system where you can access services or information
examples: Use the student portal to check your grades.
The bank launched a new customer portal.

portal.definition: a doorway or opening, often imagined in stories or science fiction
examples: In the story, the hero stepped through a portal.

portfolio.definition: a collection of a person’s work, skills, or achievements, often shown to employers
examples: She built an online portfolio for design jobs.
The artist brought a portfolio to the interview.

philanthropic.definition: connected with helping people, especially by giving money to good causes
examples: He made a philanthropic donation to the hospital.
The foundation has a philanthropic mission.

plate.definition: a flat dish used to serve food
examples: Put the pasta on the plate.
She ate from a small plate.

plate.definition: a flat piece of metal used for covering or supporting
examples: The machine parts are held by a steel plate.
A plate covers the hole.

plate.definition: to cover food with a layer of something, especially in cooking
examples: They plated the dessert neatly.
The chef plated the main course.

page.definition: one side of a paper in a book, magazine, or document
examples: Turn to page 12.
The page is missing.

page.definition: a person who helps at events by running errands or delivering messages
examples: The page handed out programs at the theater.

page.definition: to send a message to someone by electronic paging or a short alert
examples: They paged me when my turn was ready.

pig.definition: a farm animal with a pink body and a snout, raised for meat
examples: The pig looks healthy.
They raise pigs on the farm.

physician.definition: a doctor who treats illness and provides medical care
examples: The physician examined him.
She saw a physician for her symptoms.

prescribe.definition: to recommend or officially order a treatment, medicine, or course of action
examples: The doctor prescribed antibiotics.
They prescribed a strict diet.

pal.definition: a friend, used in informal speech
examples: Thanks, pal.
I met my pal at school.

portly.definition: somewhat fat in a dignified, not unhealthy, way
examples: The old man was portly.
He wore a portly suit.

peer.definition: someone with the same age or social level as you
examples: She asked for advice from a peer.
Teachers should support every peer.

peer.definition: to look closely, especially to see something that is hard to notice
examples: I peered into the dark room.
He peered through the glass.

parity.definition: a state of being equal or balanced
examples: They wanted parity between the teams.
The policy aims for parity in pay.

physique.definition: a person’s body shape and physical build
examples: He has a strong physique.
Her physique is athletic.

poppy.definition: a flower that often has bright red, pink, or orange blooms
examples: The field was full of poppies.
She picked a small poppy for the table.

portable.definition: easy to carry or move from place to place
examples: Bring a portable chair to the picnic.
The portable speaker connects by Bluetooth.

porter.definition: a person who carries luggage for travelers, especially at a hotel or station
examples: The porter brought my suitcase to the room.
We tipped the porter.

porter.definition: a person who carries goods in an industrial or shipping setting
examples: A porter works in the warehouse.

plumber.definition: a person who installs and repairs pipes and plumbing systems
examples: The plumber fixed the leak.
We called a plumber after the sink clogged.
